notes.text: The page states a reconstruction problem: recover the topological groupoid attached to a weighted graph with repères, together with its functorial dependence and the seven operations except 4° and 5°. It proposes obtaining operation 4° from an explicit description, and places hole-closing among elementary structures. This is the content of a mathematical programme, not a proof on this sheet.

The lower arrow relates the groupoid with a triple index g, nu, nu-prime to a groupoid whose second index combines nu and nu-prime. Its bracketed annotation describes X with a subset I-prime of I(X) of cardinality nu-prime. The main reader’s targeted local check is that capping nu-prime distinct selected boundary components of a compact surface with nu boundary components removes exactly those nu-prime components and leaves the genus unchanged, giving target count nu minus nu-prime. This check flags the doubtful written operator but is not an emendation: the I-shaped ink remains plus/minus first, with minus and plus alternatives. It does not prove the reconstruction programme or functorial claims.

The left NB explicitly drops S or D because these are already contained in the underlined Gamma. The later question “avec ou sans S?” is retained beside the lower arrow, and both displayed initial S letters remain visibly cancelled. These source revisions are recorded without forcing a consistent final convention.

The curved line by pourrait connects the raised insertion to the baseline; it does not provide evidence for H’s additional cancelled s’expliciteront. The lower bracket is flat, with short upward ends, and is reproduced by a TikZ path. H’s repeated T-with-triple-index and introductory colon below it are editorial expansions, not new ink.

The two page numerals are 19 at the head and a pale 62 at the foot. The lower folio annotation is assigned to an unnamed hand with attribution uncertain; its appearance alone does not establish a different writer.

Several old readings remain unresolved because cancellation obscures letters. The final ou before the S T/T pair is clear and stands outside the first-word doubt; a possible comma remains uncertain. The run replaced by structures has two separated tall/looped groups: an unreadable initial unit plus doubtful données is the leading segmentation, with the single-word reading explicitly retained as an alternative. No old word is supplied from the clear replacement.
